conventions.axes: Current Body, +x toward the nose; stations measured from the phase structural datum (base = 0).
conventions.angle: Total angle between nose axis and relative velocity, 0 (nose-first) .. pi (engine-first).
conventions.decomposition: Axial: -qbar*S_ref*CA0(M)*cos(a)*|cos(a)| along +x. Lateral: potential qbar*S_ref*CN_alpha*sin(a)*|cos(a)| plus crossflow qbar*CDc*S_side*sin(a)^2 per side segment, each along -(lateral relative velocity direction).
conventions.moments: Potential force at the windward-end station (mirrored about CG x for retro flow); crossflow force per segment at its side-area centroid; rotary damping c*qbar*S_ref*L_ref^2/(2V)*omega.
conventions.side_segments: Incremental projected widths; overlap with the body segment is intentional (fins, legs).
conventions.damping: Pitch damping applied to yaw by axisymmetry; roll damping separate. Zero means declared unmodeled.

full_stack.class: crossflow approximation over sourced axial curve
full_stack.evidence: Axial CA0: data/drag_curve_pezent_extended.json. Mach 0..7 unchanged from the Pezent 2024 Fig.2.13(b) readout (RasAeroII, 0 deg AoA, full Falcon9-like stack with 5.2 m fairing); Mach 8 and 10 knots appended as a declared estimate with slow hypersonic decay. Normal force, crossflow, damping and the potential center are declared estimates without sourced data.
full_stack.uncertainty: Axial Mach 0..7: see the original drag_curve_pezent.json record (pixel readout, transonic rise worst). Axial Mach 7..10: declared estimate; in that regime the vehicle is above roughly 55 km where drag stays below about 0.5 percent of thrust.
full_stack.notes: Applies while stage1+stage2+payload remain attached (datum: stack base = 0).

booster_alone.evidence: No sourced coefficients for the separated booster. Axial curve estimated for a blunt-ended cylinder of fineness ratio 11.6 (friction + bluff base/interstage, transonic peak), extended to Mach 10 by the same declared decay convention as the full stack. Potential slope from slender-body theory (2 per rad, referenced to the 3.66 m body cross-section). Crossflow CDc from subcritical cylinder values. Pitch damping from slender launch-vehicle order of magnitude.
booster_alone.uncertainty: Axial CA0 uncertain to roughly +/-50 percent; normal force and damping are order-of-magnitude only. The Mach 7..10 knots are declared estimates (see full_stack). Refined evidence should replace all entries.
booster_alone.notes: Separation leaves the booster in the original datum (engine bay base = 0, interstage top = 42.6). Flows either direction are approximated with the same CA0 (both ends are bluff equipment sections).

booster_landing.evidence: booster_alone estimates plus declared increments: grid fins and deployed legs add projected side area near the interstage and the engine bay, axial CA0 raised by a flat crossfin/leg increment (+0.25 subsonic, decreasing to +0.25/0.17 by Mach 7), roll damping from the grid fins.
booster_landing.uncertainty: Increments are declared estimates, not measured. Grid-fin normal force in reality is control-effective (movable); this model treats fins as fixed crossflow area only.
booster_landing.notes: Same datum as booster_alone. Fin/leg segments are incremental widths beyond the body.

grid_fin_control.evidence: Falcon 9 grid fin approximated as a porous lattice panel of about 1.5 m x 1.1 m (1.65 m2); lift slope per fin 1.2 per rad, roughly half of a solid panel of aspect ratio near one because of lattice porosity. Mount stations sit inside the declared fin side segment; maximum deflection about 20 degrees matches observed strokes. Azimuths are intercardinal (45, 135, 225, 315 degrees).
grid_fin_control.uncertainty: Order-of-magnitude declared estimate. The real fins are individually commanded and their effectiveness varies with Mach, alpha and lattice state; those dependencies are declared unmodeled, as is any deflection axial-drag increment and interference with the passive crossflow segments.
grid_fin_control.convention: Azimuth about Body +x from +y toward +z; a positive deflection pushes fin i along (0, -sin(phi), cos(phi)), scaled by the axial-flow share cos(a)*|cos(a)| (full nose-first, reversed engine-first, zero at 90 degrees total angle).

side_segments.note: four grid fins combined, incremental projected width beyond the body
deployed landing legs, incremental projected width beyond the body

second_stack.evidence: No sourced coefficients for stage 2 + Dragon. Axial curve estimated like booster_alone but sleeker (nose cone instead of bluff interstage), extended to Mach 10 by the declared decay convention; potential slope from slender-body theory; side areas from the 3.66 m stage-2 body and the 3.7 m Dragon trunk section.
second_stack.uncertainty: Order-of-magnitude declared estimates throughout; the Mach 7..10 knots are declared estimates (see full_stack). To be replaced by evidence.
second_stack.notes: After separation the upper vehicle runs in its own datum (stage-2 aft skirt base = 0, Dragon top = 19.8).

booster_return.evidence: booster_alone estimates plus declared increments: grid fins and deployed legs add projected side area near the interstage and the engine bay, axial CA0 raised by a flat crossfin/leg increment (+0.25 subsonic, decreasing to +0.25/0.17 by Mach 7), roll damping from the grid fins.
booster_return.uncertainty: Increments are declared estimates, not measured. Grid-fin normal force in reality is control-effective (movable); this model treats fins as fixed crossflow area only.
booster_return.notes: A integration configuration: B booster_landing coefficients and fins, with deployed-leg segment omitted. Fins deployed after boostback; legs deploy at landing ignition. No new measured coefficients.
